title: How much of the rectangle does the triangle cover?
description: A triangle has its base on the bottom side of a five centimetre by four centimetre rectangle and its top corner on the top side. A height splits the rectangle into two smaller rectangles, and the triangle is half of each. Keeko doubts this and says the area changes when the top corner slides.
teaching_notes: One idea: a height turns the triangle into half of two rectangles, so the triangle is half of the whole rectangle. Watch for children who think the area changes as the top corner slides.

source: X is on the top side of a rectangle with DC = 5 cm and height 4 cm. Find the area of the triangle XDC.
video_script.why: The child knows that a diagonal halves a rectangle, but this triangle is not made by a diagonal alone. A height splits the rectangle so that each part is halved by a diagonal.
video_script.substitution: Drop a height from the top corner to make two rectangles, then take half of each one and add.
video_script.anchor: the rectangle of the book, five centimetres long and four centimetres tall, with a triangle on its bottom side
video_script.wrong_answer: the area changes when the top corner slides
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the area changes when the top corner slides along the top side. Wherever it sits, the two smaller rectangles still add up to the whole one, and the triangle is half of both.
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the triangle is ten square centimetres
hold_back: the area of the triangle is 10 cm²
never_show: the area of the triangle, before the answer beat
maths_rules: rectangle with bottom side DC = 5 cm and height 4 cm; X on the top side
drop XY perpendicular to DC; XY = 4 cm; it splits the rectangle into two rectangles
XD is a diagonal of the left rectangle and XC a diagonal of the right one, so each triangle part is half its rectangle
drawn case: DY = 2 cm and YC = 3 cm: left rectangle 2 × 4 = 8, half 4; right rectangle 3 × 4 = 12, half 6; 4 + 6 = 10 cm²
area of triangle XDC = half of the whole rectangle = 1/2 × 5 × 4 = 10 cm²
wherever X sits, DY + YC = 5, so the two rectangles always fill the whole 5 by 4 rectangle
video_script.design: One idea: a height turns the triangle into two halves of rectangles. Wrong idea: the area changes as the top corner slides. The rectangle with its triangle stays on stage from the hook to the end.
